Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync; reviewed benchmark numbers vs baseline provider; identified tuning opportunities (batching, kv/prefix caching, quantization tradeoffs); agreed on follow-ups to run a focused p95 tuning and share production traces.
Topics: baseline comparison, latency p50/p95, throughput (rps / tokens/s), cost delta, tuning knobs, security/VPC questions, next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick check, can you all hear me?
[00:05] Priya (Acme): Yep, I can hear you. Sorry running a bit late, traffic.
[00:10] Jordan: No worries. Sofia and I will jump straight into the benchmark numbers we ran overnight vs your baseline provider. We uploaded the sheet to the drive and linked it in the calendar.
[00:22] Markus (Acme): Got it. we pulled the sheet, some of the column headers are a bit off, I'll flag later.
[00:28] Sofia (Redwood SE): Cool, I'll share my screen — bear with me, i'm on a hotspot so if audio drops i'll rejoin.
[00:38] Elena (Acme): Also FYI Priya's out next week so she's trying to get this aligned.

[01:05] Sofia: Ok, so quick runbook: we used your top-10 prompt set (thanks Priya), ran 3x steady-state passes at 8k context and 2k context, measured p50/p95 token-level latency, and max sustained throughput. Baseline provider is "BaselineCloudAI" numbers they gave you—right?
[01:22] Priya: Yep, baseline is BaselineCloudAI with their managed endpoints.
[01:27] Sofia: Alright first slide — p50 latency at 2k context: BaselineCloudAI = 220ms, Redwood hosted = 120ms on same V100 equivalent instance; p95: Baseline = 780ms, Redwood = 320ms. Those are median of runs, some variance.
[01:45] Markus: Wait 320ms p95, is that with batching? What batch sizes?
[01:50] Sofia: We used dynamic batching with up to 8 requests / batch, target latency SLO set to 250ms for the test, but for fairness we measured without hard SLOs. The p95 number is from typical batching config — we also include a no-batch run in the appendix.
[02:05] Jordan: to be clear, the baseline's p95 did balloon because they don't do KV prefix caching the same way; their kv cache warmed slower on long sequences. Also their model variant was 8-bit quantized but different kernel fallbacks.
[02:20] Priya: Hmm, we saw more 5xxs on baseline during the longer-run test, is that consistent?
[02:26] Sofia: yes, baseline hit occasional CPU-bound stalls under sustained throughput; Redwood's runtime has continuous batching and better kernel selection which reduces stalls. We pulled logs — i'll share the raw.

[03:00] Priya: Can you give numbers for throughput? Our QPS target is 120 rps during peak with average 160 tokens per request.
[03:08] Sofia: Sure — sustained throughput measured: BaselineCloudAI = ~75 rps at 2k context before errors increased; Redwood hosted = 135 rps sustained on the same hardware class. For 8k context, baseline dropped to ~32 rps, Redwood = 58 rps. So about 1.8–1.9x better throughput in our runs.
[03:30] Markus: That aligns with our internal sim, interesting. What about cost? Raw token unit cost?
[03:36] Jordan: Our estimate (including batching gains + prefix caching) shows unit cost reduction ~28% vs baseline for your workload. We'll send the cost/throughput spreadsheet with raw numbers.
[03:46] Elena: Are those including networking egress costs? We usually include egress for on-prem connectors.
[03:51] Jordan: Not in the sheet yet, we can add a column for egress to match your accounting.

[04:10] Markus: So what's the p95 tuning you mentioned in email?
[04:15] Sofia: We think p95 can improve further with three changes: 1) reduce max batch latency threshold for tail latency sensitive routes, 2) enable prefix/KV cache for warm sessions, 3) try 4-bit quantization profile on dev to trade minor accuracy for throughput. We want to run a focused p95 run with 8k context and a batch latency target of 20ms.
[04:35] Priya: That 4-bit quantization — we've seen hallucination increase in other tests, what's your expectation?
[04:40] Sofia: Good call — we expect slight quality delta on the most sensitive prompts, but in our evals using your prompt set, topicality and factual accuracy stayed within your acceptance thresholds for 80%+ of prompts. We'll include per-prompt deltas.

[05:10] Jordan: On security — any new concerns from your side about private deployment? You'd mentioned VPC peering and KMS earlier.
[05:17] Priya: Yes SOC 2 is table stakes, but we need customer-managed KMS and audit logs to integrate into our SIEM. Also residency: some data must stay in eu-west for GDPR.
[05:28] Jordan: Redwood Private supports customer KMS/HSM and we can pin region. We'll attach our SOC 2 and ISO artifacts and a short architecture note for VPC peering.
[05:38] Markus: For the on-prem option, what about the required GPU footprint? We can't spare more than two 80GB cards initially.
[05:44] Sofia: We can run a constrained config: model sharding + model-quantization to fit two 80GB A100s for inference with some throughput tradeoffs. We'll draft a sizing note after we see your production traces.

[06:15] Elena: A couple quick questions from product: does Redwood support function/tool calling or long-loop state across turns? We have multi-turn flows.
[06:23] Jordan: Yes, we have streaming + function calling semantics; for long-loop we rely on KV cache and you can persist the minimal state in your service. We'll share an example pattern.

[07:00] Priya: About the baseline numbers — we need the raw logs to do apples-to-apples. Can you share the raw latency traces and the configs you used?
[07:07] Sofia: Absolutely, sheet has links to logs and the runner config; note some of the baseline labels got munged by their agent, e.g. 'K-V cash' in one log — so ignore typos.
[07:18] Markus: haha yeah, their transcript said 'K V cash' too.

[08:00] Jordan: Ok let's talk risks: two things — quality regression on aggressive quantization, and network egress in private deployment. We'll mitigate with canaryed rollouts and per-prompt evals.
[08:12] Priya: What's Redwood's recommended canary % for this workload?
[08:17] Sofia: Start with 5% traffic for 24 hours, run automated quality checks on your top prompts and then 20% for 12 hours, then full. We'll supply the rollout policy template.

[09:00] Elena: Any competitor angles? We heard BaselineCloudAI is pushing a new kernel set with improved batching — did you run against that?
[09:07] Sofia: We used their supplied endpoint version from last week; if they pushed a new kernel, numbers could change — but our advantage is kernel selection + continuous batching + prefix caching combined, which is independent. We'll rerun if you want.

[10:00] Jordan: Quick demo of the dashboard — showing per-route p50/p95 and token cost, can you see my screen?
[10:06] Markus: yes. the route-level breakdown is helpful.
[10:15] Jordan: Here you can toggle baseline overlay; also see a per-token cost heatmap.

[12:20] Sofia: One note on measurement: p95 can be noisy for low QPS routes; we aggregated over a 10min steady window and excluded warm-up. Details in appendix.

[15:00] Priya: ok good, so what's the ask for this week?
[15:05] Jordan: Action items: we'll send the raw logs + spreadsheet, Sofia will run the p95 tuning run and share results, and Acme will provide production traces. We'll also slot an architecture workshop for private deployment.

[15:25] Elena: timeline ok. If we get the production trace by Tues, can you size the private cluster by Friday?
[15:32] Sofia: yes we can do a preliminary sizing by Friday.

[17:00] Priya: one more — do you have any compliance checklist for our procurement/legal team?
[17:06] Jordan: yes, i'll attach the compliance pack (SOC2, contract SLAs, DPA) in the follow-up email.

[20:00] Jordan: Recap / Next steps: Jordan send benchmark + pricing (due 10/15), Sofia run p95 tuning and share configs (due 10/16), Priya share traces and prompts (due 10/20), schedule workshop (week of 10/26).
[20:20] Priya: thanks everyone.
[20:28] Markus: thanks.
[20:33] Elena: bye.

(Transcript ends; some speaker labels may be slightly off from recording.)
